declarations.description: Themes PIE content by resolving the `--pie-*` tokens and writing them inline, with `data-theme`, `data-color-scheme` and `color-scheme`, on its target: itself under `scope="self"`, `documentElement` under `scope="document"`. Layers apply in order base theme, provider adapter output, registered color scheme, then `variables`, and the element re-resolves when the OS color scheme (under `theme="auto"`), the provider registry or the scheme catalog changes. It renders nothing of its own and defaults to `display: contents`.
declarations.name: PieThemeElement

members.name: theme
members.description: Base theme: `light` (default), `dark`, or `auto` to follow `prefers-color-scheme`; another attribute value, such as a DaisyUI theme name, becomes `data-theme` over the light base.

members.name: scope
members.description: Write target: `self` (default) for this element, or `document` for `documentElement`, where the most recently connected or changed document-scoped `<pie-theme>` is active.

members.name: variables
members.description: Explicit overrides, the last layer: `--*` keys with string or finite-number values, mirrored to the `variables` attribute as JSON.

members.name: provider
members.description: Provider adapter to read host tokens through: a registered adapter id, `auto` (default) for the first registered adapter that can read the target, or `none`.

members.name: scheme
members.description: Requested color scheme id; `default` (default) applies none, and an id not yet registered is kept and applies once a matching scheme registers.

cssProperties.name: --pie-disabled-text
cssProperties.description: Canonical foreground for text that is disabled but still has to be read - a non-editable label rather than a control - held to the 4.5:1 text minimum against --pie-background rather than the 3:1 --pie-disabled answers to as a state fill. Must fall back through canonical --pie-text so a host that themes only the canonical text token gets full contrast rather than an unreadable literal.

cssProperties.name: --pie-fixed-hue-collapse
cssProperties.description: Share, as a percentage, by which a component's own fixed hues collapse into the palette's surface and ink. Not a colour: a component mixes its fixed value towards --pie-background-dark and --pie-text by this share, so 0% keeps the hue exactly as authored and 100% removes it. Base Themes set 0%; every colour scheme sets 100%, because a two-colour palette is a promise a fixed hue breaks -- the periodic table's category fills are the first consumer. A palette that keeps hue encodings must set 0% explicitly; a registered custom scheme that says nothing collapses them.
